translationRepairs: When Emperor Huan's Longxi prefect Feng Huan first took office and opened his seal box, two crimson snakes shot out, one south, one north.
When Emperor Huan's Longxi prefect Feng Gun first took office and opened his seal box, two crimson snakes shot out, one south, one north.
s0049 names 陇西太守冯绲; 绲 is Gun, so Feng Huan is a false reading of the given name and Feng Gun is the accurate repair.
Under Emperor Huan, when Feng Huan had first received appointment as grand administrator of Longxi, he opened the case for his seal-cord, and two red snakes divided, going south and north.
Under Emperor Huan, when Feng Gun had first received appointment as grand administrator of Longxi, he opened the case for his seal-cord, and two red snakes divided, going south and north.
The same unit has 冯绲; the literal Feng Huan repeats the misreading of 绲 as Huan, and Feng Gun restores the supported personal name.

Huan had Man cast the stalks. When the pattern formed, Man said, "Three years hence you will hold a border command; your title will contain the word 'east,' and you will campaign three thousand li toward the northeast.

Gun had Man cast the stalks. When the pattern formed, Man said, "Three years hence you will hold a border command; your title will contain the word 'east,' and you will campaign three thousand li toward the northeast.
s0050 opens 绲令曼筮之, continuing the Longxi grand administrator 冯绲 of s0049; the subject is Gun, not Emperor Huan or a man named Huan.

Huan ordered Man to cast milfoil for it; when the hexagram was complete, Man said, "After three years you will become a general on the frontier, your office will have 'east' in its name, and you ought to march three thousand li toward the northeast.

Gun ordered Man to cast milfoil for it; when the hexagram was complete, Man said, "After three years you will become a general on the frontier, your office will have 'east' in its name, and you ought to march three thousand li toward the northeast.
Literal likewise turns subject 绲 into Huan; Gun ordered Man to cast milfoil matches the Chinese agent.

In the first year of the Yanxi era Huan went out as grand administrator of Liaodong and attacked the Xianbei; by the fifth year he was again appointed general of chariots and cavalry and struck the Wuling Man bandits—everything was as divined.

In the first year of the Yanxi era Gun went out as grand administrator of Liaodong and attacked the Xianbei; by the fifth year he was again appointed general of chariots and cavalry and struck the Wuling Man bandits—everything was as divined.
s0052 has 绲出为辽东太守; the man who went out as Liaodong grand administrator is again Feng Gun, so Gun is required.
Yanxi 3 saw the Langye rebel Lao Bing and the Taishan rebel Sun Wuji murder a commandant.
Yanxi 3 saw the Langye rebel Lao Bing and the Taishan rebel Shusun Wuji murder a commandant.
s0056 names 太山贼叔孙无忌; 叔孙 is the compound surname Shusun, so Sun Wuji drops 叔 and yields a different name.
In the third year of the Yanxi era the Langye bandit Lao Bing and the Taishan bandit Sun Wuji killed a commandant.
In the third year of the Yanxi era the Langye bandit Lao Bing and the Taishan bandit Shusun Wuji killed a commandant.
The literal of the same sentence likewise truncates 叔孙无忌 to Sun Wuji; Shusun Wuji restores the full compound surname.
The court named Zong Zi of Nanyang bandit-quelling general-in-chief, gave him the ceremonial axe, and ordered him to coordinate commandery forces against Sun Wuji.
The court named Zong Zi of Nanyang bandit-quelling general-in-chief, gave him the ceremonial axe, and ordered him to coordinate commandery forces against Shusun Wuji.
s0058 合讨无忌 refers back to 叔孙无忌 of s0056; expanding 无忌 as Sun Wuji invents the wrong surname, while Shusun Wuji correctly identifies him.
Fan Zhizhang was from Nanzhong in Hanzhong.
Fan Zhizhang was from Nanzheng in Hanzhong.
s0063 has 汉中南郑人; 南郑 is Nanzheng in Hanzhong, not the far-southwest region 南中 (Nanzhong).
Fan Zhizhang was a man of Nanzhong in Hanzhong.
Fan Zhizhang was a man of Nanzheng in Hanzhong.
Literal of the same unit likewise misreads 南郑 as Nanzhong; Nanzheng is the place-name supported by the Chinese.

Prefectural mansions summoned him ten times, the coach office thrice, and he twice received nominations as worthy, good, incorrupt, erudite, and possessed of the Way—each time he pleaded illness and stayed home.

The offices of the chief ministers summoned him ten times, the coach office thrice, and he twice received nominations as worthy, good, incorrupt, erudite, and possessed of the Way—each time he pleaded illness and stayed home.
s0096 宰府十辟 are summonses by the chief ministers' offices at court, not by local prefectural mansions; the proposed wording matches that sense.
A midwife reached in and drew out a black, recognizable stillbirth.
He had someone probe for it, and out came a black, recognizable stillbirth.
s0170 使人探之 says Hua Tuo had someone probe for the dead fetus; the original invents a midwife the Chinese does not name.

He split the leftover powder for Li. Five years later a neighbor with the same cough begged desperately; Li, moved, gave up his store, then rode to Qiao for more—only to find Tuo in chains, too ashamed to ask.

He split the leftover powder for Li. Five or six years later a neighbor with the same cough begged desperately; Li, moved, gave up his store, then rode to Qiao for more—only to find Tuo in chains, too ashamed to ask.
s0182 后五六岁 is an approximate 'after five or six years'; 'Five years later' falsely states a definite count the text does not give.
Dismissed with a bamboo staff, he was told, "Straddle this and wish yourself anywhere—you will arrive.
Zhangfang took leave to return; the old man gave him a bamboo staff, saying, "Ride this wherever you wish to go, and you will arrive of yourself.
s0246 has 长房辞归，翁与一竹杖，曰; the original drops both named agents and turns the old man's gift into a passive dismissal, while the proposed wording restores the subjects and gift.
He once dandled a neighbor's infant, dropped it to the ground, and killed it; the parents howled while he muttered only an apology, then helped them bury the corpse.
He once held a neighbor's infant and purposely let it fall to the ground so that it died; the parents cried out in grief while he only apologized for a mistake, and then they buried it.

s0274 故失手墯地而死 marks an intentional drop (故); the original reads as a mere accident and invents Zixun helping with the burial, while the proposed wording restores intention and has the parents bury the child.
Heading 计子勋 is a different man from earlier 蓟子训; identical unmarked Ji Zixun conflates them, and Ji Zixūn marks 勋 (xūn) to keep the English distinct.
Literal of the same heading likewise conflates 计子勋 with 蓟子训 under one spelling; Ji Zixūn is the matching disambiguation.
Ji Zixun's home county is lost; folk said he paced a few hundred steps at a time as he wandered among them.
Ji Zixūn's home county is lost; folk said he paced a few hundred steps at a time as he wandered among them.
s0329 continues 计子勋者; reusing unmarked Ji Zixun again collapses him into 蓟子训, so Ji Zixūn is required for consistency with the accepted heading repair.
This edition's heading unit reads 刘和平, but the biography body is 北海王和平 and standard witnesses title the section 王和平; Wang Heping is the supported personal name for the English heading.
Literal heading should likewise follow the body and standard-edition name Wang Heping rather than the corrupt heading graph 刘.
